title: POC decision heuristics & scope — Frostline Systems
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide hosted vs dedicated vs private for Frostline's document summarization and search assistant. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy regressions), workload sizing (peak RPS, avg tokens), benchmark plan (warm vs cold cache, KV hit rates), security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering), and a proposed 6-week POC timeline with a 2-week benchmarking sprint.

Redwood SE to prepare Private deployment checklist and KMS options (by 2027-05-14)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-08
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz — Redwood; Priya Kapoor, Ethan Ross, Lena Ortiz, Tom Bennett — Frostline

Auto-summary: Quick intro, then dove into what metrics matter for Frostline (latency, cost per 1k tokens, model accuracy), then workload sizing and benchmarking approach. Security gating questions came up around KMS/HSM and VPC peering. Ended with explicit next steps and a 6-week POC timeline proposed.

---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we're all here? quick audio check.
[00:10] Priya: Yep, hi! I can hear, thanks Maya.
[00:15] Maya: Great, so the goal for today is to scope a POC that helps you decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for the doc summarization assistant. We'll focus on success criteria, workload sizing, and a benchmark plan.
[00:28] Ethan: Sounds good. To give more context, our current infra runs on MajorCloud VMs, and we have a small internal on-prem cluster for sensitive workloads. The main questions are latency under peak, unit cost, and whether we need full VPC isolation.
[00:44] Daniel (SE): Hi all, I'll drive the benchmark design. Quick clarifying question: when you say "latency under peak", is that p95 or p99 you're optimizing for?
[00:52] Priya: p95 is our target, ideally <200ms for short prompts (~64 tokens). For longer documents we accept higher, but p95 is the primary metric for interactive UX.
[01:04] Lena: And to add, product wants consistent sub-200ms for 70% of queries, the rest can be batching. We also track cost per 1k tokens, we're aiming for under $0.45 per 1k tokens for the inference portion.
[01:19] Tom: Security: we need SOC2 compliance and audit logs, plus KMS integration. If we go Private, we need HSM/KMS option. If hosted, we need to understand key isolation.
[01:31] Maya: Perfect. So success criteria we're hearing: p95 latency target, cost per 1k token, and clear security posture. We'll translate that into concrete tests.
[01:40] Daniel: For workload sizing, can you share expected concurrency? RPS? average and peak tokens per request?
[01:48] Priya: Typical concurrency 60 active users during business hours, spike to ~320 concurrent sessions during batch runs. Average 430 tokens per request when they attach a doc, but interactive snippets are 50–90 tokens. Peak throughput target is about 120 requests/sec during batch ingestion windows, sustained for ~10 minutes.
[02:11] Daniel: Ok that's helpful. So rough numbers — 120 RPS peak, avg tokens 430 for doc flows but UI interactions are small. That affects batching strategy: dedicated pools handle sustained throughput better, hosted can be fine for bursty but unit cost varies.
[02:26] Ethan: We run in us-west and eu-west, data residency matters for eu customers. Any notes on region fallbacks?
[02:33] Maya: Redwood supports region routing. For POC we suggest benchmarking in us-west and one eu region. If you need strict data residency, Private deployment is the safest.
[02:41] Priya: Okay. Benchmarks — what do you recommend we measure?
[02:45] Daniel: We'll run a two-week benchmark sprint. Phase 1: synthetic load to verify capacity and latency (cold start + warm). Phase 2: replay of your traffic (you provide anonymized logs) to measure real-world behavior. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation, tokens/sec per GPU, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate impact, cold-start penalty, and failure rates. Also measure tail latency under continuous batching.
[03:12] Lena: How do you characterize KV caching? Our system often reuses context for follow-up prompts.
[03:17] Daniel: We track prefix/KV cache hit rate — high hit rates reduce per-token compute dramatically. We'll instrument cache-hit vs miss scenarios in the benchmark. For Redwood Dedicated we can pin warmed workers and get much better tail latencies. For Hosted we rely on runtime warm pools and autoscaling; that can be fine but you may see more variance.
[03:36] Maya: Also want to call out quantization impact. If you opt for 4-bit quantized models we can reduce cost and increase throughput, but need to validate quality with your evaluation prompts.
[03:47] Priya: Important: we must not regress on summary quality. We'll provide a small eval set to check ROUGE and human acceptability.
[03:55] Daniel: Perfect. We'll include a quality regression test as part of the benchmark: run the same prompts across model variants (fp16, int8/4bit) and flag any measurable drop beyond your tolerance.
[04:06] Tom: On the security side, if we do Hosted we need SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS, and audit log retention to 7 years. Is that supported?
[04:18] Maya: Hosted supports SAML and audit logs; KMS options exist but for full customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys we'd steer you toward Private or Dedicated with a managed KMS integration. We'll send the security matrix.
[04:33] Ethan: What's the expected timeline to run the POC and have a decision?
[04:37] Maya: We typically propose 6 weeks: week 0 prep and data collection, weeks 1–2 benchmarking sprint (synthetic + replay), week 3 analysis and quality checks, week 4 pilot cutover in a single region, week 5 multi-region validation, week 6 decision and next-phase contract negotiation. If you want an accelerated path, we can reduce to 4 weeks but it increases risk.
[05:01] Priya: 6 weeks sounds reasonable. We need the ability to do a canary with a subset of users.
[05:06] Daniel: Canary is standard — we'll show you routing rules and rollout percent.
[05:10] Lena: A few nitty-gritty questions — do we get token-level cost breakdowns per route/model? We want visibility into which flows are driving cost.
[05:19] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards. We'll include sample screenshots in the follow-up.
[05:26] Ethan: On dedicated capacity — does that guarantee fixed GPUs, and what's burst behavior?
[05:32] Daniel: Dedicated reserves capacity so you get predictable throughput. Burst can be configured as a buffer, but there's a cost tradeoff. For predictable 120 RPS sustained peaks during ingestion windows, Dedicated makes sense. Hosted can handle it too but you pay for the autoscale delta.
[05:50] Priya: Pricing question — can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated monthly costs for our estimated load?
[05:55] Maya: We'll model it and send a worksheet. Roughly, if your workload needs consistent high throughput, Dedicated tends to be cheaper per token. Hosted has lower startup friction. We'll include cost per 1k tokens and expected monthly bill in the worksheet.
[06:09] Tom: Data handling: if we route EU traffic to EU region but model weights come from a global repo, is that a compliance issue?
[06:17] Daniel: For Private we'd ensure weights and inference run entirely inside your VPC or on-prem host. For Hosted we can restrict data residency, but exact requirements around model weights may need legal review. We'll note this as a gating question.
[06:29] Priya: Benchmarks — do you run cold-start scenarios with container spin-up times? We had very long cold starts previously.
[06:35] Daniel: Yes, tests include cold-start latency and sustained warm latency. We'll instrument start-to-first-token times and p99 during scale-up events. Also measure impact of continuous batching window sizes on tail latency.
[06:47] Ethan: For the replay, what format do you need?
[06:50] Daniel: JSONL with timestamp, prompt, token count, and anonymous user id is ideal. We can provide a template.
[06:57] Maya: Quick note — if you want Private, we'll need network details and a support timeline for on-prem setup. That typically adds 2–4 weeks of provisioning beyond the 6-week plan.
[07:09] Lena: Understood. Our preference is to evaluate Hosted and Dedicated first, then consider Private if security gating requires it.
[07:15] Priya: Ok that makes sense. A couple of other concerns: model upgrades — we need rollback strategy if new model introduces regressions.
[07:22] Daniel: Rollouts and rollback are built into Redwood Console — canary percentages, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval set. We'll demo that in the pilot.
[07:33] Tom: About audit logs and retention — are logs exported to customer S3?
[07:36] Maya: Yes, you can forward logs to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include export options in the security doc.
[07:45] Speaker 6: (inaudible) ... sorry missed last part, can you repeat logging export?
[07:50] Maya: Sure, logs can be streamed to your cloud storage or pushed to Splunk/Datadog.
[07:56] Daniel: Also want to highlight benchmarking scenarios we recommend: 1) interactive small prompts 50–90 tokens, 2) doc-extraction 400–900 tokens, 3) burst ingestion at 120 RPS. Each with cold and warm caches.
[08:15] Priya: Quality guardrails — we will define an acceptability threshold. If int8 or 4-bit quant causes >5% drop in human acceptability we'll mark it as not acceptable.
[08:25] Daniel: We'll capture that.
[08:27] Maya: Anything else on the success criteria side?
[08:29] Priya: Also SLA needs — 99.5% uptime and <1% error rate for production. For POC we can accept slightly lower but must baseline the error modes.
[08:40] Daniel: We'll measure error rates and classify by type (server error, OOM, context truncation).
[08:46] Lena: Can we test multi-region failover? We have EU failover requirements.
[08:50] Maya: Yes, that will be part of the later pilot weeks. We'll plan a simulated regional outage test.
[08:58] Ethan: Any blockers from Redwood side to do the two-week sprint?
[09:02] Daniel: We need the anonymized traffic and a sample of your evaluation prompts (for quality checks). Also credentials for the test S3 and per-region endpoints if you want region-local testing.
[09:12] Priya: We'll gather those.
[09:15] Maya: Ok I'll recap next steps at the end. Anything else?
[09:19] (short pause)
[09:22] Tom: One more on compliance — what certifications do you hold? SOC2 Type II, ISO?
[09:27] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. We'll attach certs and a short security FAQ. For Private on-prem deployments we provide a hardened package and support guide.
[09:38] Lena: Great.
[09:40] Daniel: We'll also include a simple benchmarking script that runs with locust/gatling or a node tool, and a spreadsheet to track p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[09:53] Priya: Timeline acceptance from our side: we commit to provide data artifacts by 2027-05-13 and will aim to start the sprint 2027-05-17.
[09:59] Maya: Excellent. We'll send the template and a proposed 6-week plan.
[10:04] (cross-talk)
[10:10] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood sends benchmark template, pricing worksheet, security docs; customer provides anonymized traffic and eval prompts; schedule kickoff for 2027-05-17. Action items captured in the notes. Any objections?
[10:22] Priya: No objections, sounds good.
[10:25] Ethan: Good.
[10:27] Lena: Thanks all.
[10:29] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[10:32] (meeting ends)

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Key technical decision drivers: tail latency (p95 target <200ms for short prompts), cost per 1k tokens target <$0.45, quality regressions threshold (human acceptability drop <=5%).
- Preferred evaluation order: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (if security gating requires).
- Benchmark sprint: 2 weeks replay + synthetic, instruments for cache-hit rates and cold-starts.

References mentioned during call:
- Benchmark template (link to be shared)
- Security matrix and SOC2 certs (link to be shared)
- Pricing worksheet (link to be shared)

Potential risks called out:
- Cold-start tail latency causing UX regressions if Hosted pools are not warmed
- Compliance gating on KMS/HSM could require Private deployment and add time
- Quantization may reduce cost but requires manual quality validation

Decision gate criteria for finish of POC:
- Benchmarks show p95 for interactive flows <200ms in preferred region OR a clear mitigation path with dedicated pools
- Cost model shows viable unit economics at expected monthly volume OR roadmap to Dedicated to optimize cost
- No critical security gaps: KMS and audit log requirements satisfied or Private is approved
